{
  "dataset_name": "spambase",
  "model_family": "linear_svm",
  "schema_generator": "gemini-3.1-pro-preview",
  "schema_version": "1.0",
  "features": [
    {
      "name": "log_capital_total",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Log-transformed total number of capital letters to compress the long tail and provide a smooth continuous feature for linear margins.",
      "value_range": [0.69, 9.22],
      "feature_family": "magnitude_scaling",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Reduces the impact of extreme outliers in capital letter counts, allowing the SVM to learn a more stable weight.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "np.log1p(capital_run_length_total)"
    },
    {
      "name": "log_capital_longest",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Log-transformed length of the longest continuous sequence of capital letters.",
      "value_range": [0.69, 9.22],
      "feature_family": "magnitude_scaling",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Provides a normalized severity measure of capitalization bursts, which is highly informative for linear decision boundaries.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "np.log1p(capital_run_length_longest)"
    },
    {
      "name": "capital_burstiness",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Ratio of the longest capital run to the average capital run, clipped to a maximum of 50.",
      "value_range": [0.0, 50.0],
      "feature_family": "ratio",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Captures the relative extremity of capitalization within the text, providing a scale-invariant feature useful for linear models.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "np.clip(capital_run_length_longest / np.maximum(capital_run_length_average, 1.0), 0.0, 50.0)"
    },
    {
      "name": "total_special_chars_log",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Log-transformed sum of all special character frequencies.",
      "value_range": [0.0, 5.0],
      "feature_family": "composite_scaling",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Aggregates sparse character frequencies into a single dense, smooth feature that linear models can easily weight.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "np.log1p(char_freq_0 + char_freq_1 + char_freq_2 + char_freq_3 + char_freq_4 + char_freq_5)"
    },
    {
      "name": "char_freq_3_dominance",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "The proportion of special character frequency 3 relative to all special characters.",
      "value_range": [0.0, 1.0],
      "feature_family": "proportion",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Provides a bounded [0,1] ratio that isolates the specific impact of one highly variable character frequency against the overall character usage.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "char_freq_3 / np.maximum(char_freq_0 + char_freq_1 + char_freq_2 + char_freq_3 + char_freq_4 + char_freq_5, 0.01)"
    },
    {
      "name": "frequent_words_sum_log",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Log-transformed sum of several high-frequency words to create a dense composite feature.",
      "value_range": [0.0, 5.0],
      "feature_family": "composite_scaling",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Combines multiple correlated high-frequency word features into a single smooth projection, reducing collinearity issues in linear SVMs.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "np.log1p(word_freq_11 + word_freq_18 + word_freq_20 + word_freq_24 + word_freq_26)"
    },
    {
      "name": "rare_words_sum_log",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Log-transformed sum of several low-frequency words.",
      "value_range": [0.0, 3.0],
      "feature_family": "composite_scaling",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Aggregates sparse signals from rare words into a continuous measure, improving the margin separation for edge cases.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "np.log1p(word_freq_3 + word_freq_37 + word_freq_46)"
    },
    {
      "name": "word_freq_18_26_diff",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Absolute difference between two highly variable word frequencies.",
      "value_range": [0.0, 25.0],
      "feature_family": "difference",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Captures the divergence between two common vocabulary terms, providing an interaction-like effect in a linear space.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "np.abs(word_freq_18 - word_freq_26)"
    },
    {
      "name": "char_freq_4_scaled",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Scaled and clipped version of character frequency 4.",
      "value_range": [0.0, 1.0],
      "feature_family": "normalization",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Bounds the feature strictly between 0 and 1, which is ideal for SVM regularization and margin stability.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "np.clip(char_freq_4, 0.0, 5.0) / 5.0"
    },
    {
      "name": "capital_run_length_average_scaled",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Scaled and clipped version of the average capital run length.",
      "value_range": [0.01, 1.0],
      "feature_family": "normalization",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Prevents extreme average run lengths from dominating the linear gradient updates by capping and scaling the value.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "np.clip(capital_run_length_average, 1.0, 100.0) / 100.0"
    },
    {
      "name": "semantic_urgency_score",
      "type": "judgment",
      "description": "A semantic assessment of the text's urgency or call-to-action intensity, based on the underlying vocabulary and punctuation patterns.",
      "value_range": [0.0, 1.0],
      "feature_family": "semantic_assessment",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Provides a high-level continuous severity measure of urgency that linear models can use as a strong primary axis for separation.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true
    },
    {
      "name": "semantic_commercial_intent",
      "type": "judgment",
      "description": "A semantic assessment of the likelihood that the text contains commercial, promotional, or transactional intent.",
      "value_range": [0.0, 1.0],
      "feature_family": "semantic_assessment",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Distills complex vocabulary interactions into a single linear projection representing commercial nature, directly aiding the SVM margin.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true
    }
  ]
}
